package com.termux.terminal;

/**
 * Implementation of wcwidth(3) for Unicode 15.
 *
 * Implementation from https://github.com/jquast/wcwidth but we return 0 for unprintable characters.
 *
 * IMPORTANT:
 * Must be kept in sync with the following:
 * https://github.com/termux/wcwidth
 * https://github.com/termux/libandroid-support
 * https://github.com/termux/termux-packages/tree/master/packages/libandroid-support

public final class WcWidth {

    // From https://github.com/jquast/wcwidth/blob/master/wcwidth/table_zero.py

G005_termux = Termux Android terminal emulator. ~197 Java + 67 XML; modules: app, terminal-emulator, terminal-view, termux-shared (152 files, biggest). Full app is **unbuildable here** — needs Android SDK + Gradle + network. See [[project_g_units_github_repos]].

**Verifiable core:** `terminal-emulator/src/main/java/com/termux/terminal/` has 5 pure-Java (no `import android`) classes: `WcWidth`, `TextStyle`, `ByteQueue`, `TerminalRow`, `TerminalBuffer`. Of these, WcWidth/TextStyle/ByteQueue/TerminalRow have JUnit3-style (`junit.framework.TestCase`) tests under `src/test/java` that compile+run with plain `javac` + the gradle-bundled `junit-4.13.2.jar`. The rest of the test suite (TerminalTestCase-based) pulls in the Android-dependent TerminalEmulator/TerminalSession.

**Standalone harness** (golden baseline = 34 tests OK): `/tmp/tev/verify.sh`. Needs a tiny stub `/tmp/tev/stub/.../TerminalEmulator.java` providing only `UNICODE_REPLACEMENT_CHAR=0xFFFD` (TerminalRowTest references it). junit jar lives in `~/.gradle/wrapper/dists/gradle-8.10.2-*/lib/`. TextStyleTest is exhaustive (all 259 color indices, 24-bit, all effect combos); TerminalRowTest = 187 assertions over ascii/unicode/wide/surrogate/combining/overwrite/growth.

**Refactors done (verified, 34/34 pass):**
1. `TerminalRow.setChar` — extracted duplicated grow-and-shift-tail logic (two near-identical array-realloc blocks) into one `private char[] shiftTail(text, from, count)` helper (signed count: +right/-left, grows by mColumns on overflow, updates mText). setChar shrank ~15 lines.
2. `TextStyle` — replaced repeated magic numbers (shift 40/16, mask `0b111111111L`, `0x00ffffffL`, `0xff000000`) with named constants FOREGROUND_COLOR_SHIFT/BACKGROUND_COLOR_SHIFT/COLOR_INDEX_MASK/TRUECOLOR_MASK/TRUECOLOR_ALPHA. Left the effect masks (`0b111111111` 9-bit in encode, `0b11111111111` 11-bit in decodeEffect) as literals — semantically distinct from color masks.

content.text:
I reviewed the test-covered core again and applied one more verified refactor, plus assessed what's left.

## This pass

**Refactor applied (verified, 34/34 tests pass):**

**`TerminalRow.findStartOfColumn`** — The combining-character skip loop re-implemented surrogate decoding and width-checking inline across a 13-line nested `if/else` block. `WcWidth` already exposes `width(char[], index)`, which handles the surrogate decode internally, so I collapsed it to:

```java
// Skip any zero-width (e.g. combining) chars that belong to this column.
while (newCharIndex < mSpaceUsed && WcWidth.width(mText, newCharIndex) <= 0) {
    newCharIndex += Character.isHighSurrogate(mText[newCharIndex]) ? 2 : 1;
}
```

Same behavior (break on width > 0, else advance by the surrogate-aware char count), 13 lines → 4, and it now reuses the canonical width helper instead of duplicating its logic.

## Opportunities I evaluated and deliberately skipped

- **`TerminalBuffer`** (pure-Java, ~the largest emulator class) — its tests extend `TerminalTestCase`, which instantiates the Android-dependent `TerminalEmulator`, so I can't verify changes in this offline harness. Refactoring it would be blind; not worth the regression risk.
- **Inline surrogate-decode in `copyInterval` / `wideDisplayCharacterStartingAt`** — these need *both* the decoded code point *and* to advance the index as a side effect. A clean Java helper would require out-params or an allocated object, which would hurt readability/performance more than the duplication costs. Left as-is.
- **`TextStyle` effect masks** (`0b111111111` / `0b11111111111`) — semantically distinct from the color masks I named last pass; naming them risks implying a relationship that doesn't exist. Left as literals.
- **`WcWidth` tables** — generated and must stay in sync with upstream; off-limits.
- **`ByteQueue`** — already clean; no meaningful dedup.

Net for this session: `+4 / −13` in one file, fully verified. The readily-verifiable, genuinely-improving surface in the test-covered core is now essentially exhausted across the three refactors; further work would mean either cosmetic churn or unverifiable changes to Android-coupled code, neither of which I'd recommend.
